mechanism: Classify markets by characteristic chart shape: secondary equities show short rollbacks on rises and long ones on falls, small band ranges, quiet after growth, slow rise/fast fall; commodities show explicit trends, hitches, wide ranges, more symmetric or even fast-rise/slow-fall. Treat each market type as having its own typical portrait rather than applying one indicator set across classes.
data_needed: OHLC histories labeled by asset class (equity, commodity, FX); qualitative features of rollback asymmetry, range width, hitch/break frequency.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: LUKOIL and Russian Unified Electrical Company on MICEX (May 2003–May 2004); Brent oil futures; petroleum futures; natural gas spot; Nickel cash LME; FOREX mentioned as hybrid; yearly/daily chart scales.
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an asset-class regime prior from chart morphology asymmetry instead of assuming universal TA indicators across stocks/commodities/FX.
quote: I consider every market type to have its own typical portrait.

mechanism: Reject peak-day-only volume rules (e.g. new peak on lower volume → short). In secondary stock markets, trends usually come from large traders whose activity spans many days, so interpret volume over the multi-day path around extrema, not only the extremum bar.
data_needed: Daily (or bar) volume series around price peaks/troughs; multi-day cumulative/path volume, not single extremum-day volume.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Secondary stock market examples; RSI divergence charts on equities; day-scale volume.
why_new_for_mis: Reframes volume confirmation as a multi-day large-participant activity sensor rather than classical single-bar peak-volume rules.
quote: in a second stock market trends most frequently develop as a result of large traders' activities that don't show themselves within one (even peak) day, but within many days.

mechanism: Explains betting martingale, mathematical martingale process, and FX 'spiking' MM (tiny TP / huge SL); risk/MM advice only—no market-state sensor.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: money-management / fairness theory, not MIS sensing.
quote: no reasonable strategy can help to earn money using martingale.

mechanism: Tutorial to add Alert/PlaySound/Comment/Print blocks to MACD, Stochastic, AC, Parabolic, Fractals with PrevSignal/PrevTime filters—UI alerting, not sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any chart symbol/period via Symbol()/Period(); SIGNAL_BAR=1 or 2.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: MQL4 alert plumbing tutorial only.
quote: there is nothing complicated in adding an alerting block into indicators - everyone can do this.

mechanism: Replace calendar-time bars with operational time: bars of fixed tick count (e.g. 1000 ticks) so the price process becomes statistically more homogeneous (closer to constant average deviation), enabling ordinary indicators to behave more stably across sessions; alternatively reweight calendar-time indicators by expected tick intensity.
data_needed: Tick stream or tick-volume per bar; ability to build fixed-N-tick bars or tick-count-weighted windows.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Intraday FX (EURUSD, USDJPY, USDZAR shown); H1 for ExpectedVolume tests; M1–M5 noted for volume-weighted SMA II.
why_new_for_mis: Supplies MIS a devolatilizing time transform so session-driven heteroskedasticity does not masquerade as regime change in time-bound sensors.
quote: it would be natural to use bars not with time division, but simply with a fixed number of ticks, i. e. a bar contains not 60 minutes but for example 1000 ticks.

mechanism: ExpectedVolume indicator: for each clock hour, average historical tick-volume over hist_steps prior same-hour observations (step span days; span=5 for weekday independence). Profile shows three session activity peaks (Asian, European, American); stable across neighboring weeks.
data_needed: H1 (or other intraday) tick-volume; TimeHour alignment; hist_steps (~100), span (1 or 5 days).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD and USDJPY H1 profiles; USDZAR for quiet-period illustration; parameters hist_steps=100, span=1 or 5.
why_new_for_mis: Builds an empirical intraday volatility/activity clock from tick intensity by hour—session regime scaffolding for MIS.
quote: They vividly show three peaks of trading sessions' activity - Asian, European and American.

mechanism: Corrected volumes = actual bar tick-volume / ExpectedVolume for that hour. Deviation above/below 1 flags unusually high/low market activity relative to the historical same-hour baseline.
data_needed: Current Volume[] and ExpectedVolume same-hour average.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Same FX intraday H1 setup as ExpectedVolume; Corrected_Volumes.mq4 attached.
why_new_for_mis: Turns raw tick volume into a session-normalized activity anomaly sensor usable as a liquidity/participation cue.
quote: actual volumes are divided by expected ones. So the deviation into this or that side from 1 of this indicator reflects the increased/decreased activity on the market.

mechanism: How-to for Windows Terminal Services Client from Pocket PC over Wi-Fi to control a PC running MT4—ops/remote access only.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: remote-desktop setup guide, no market sensing.
quote: We have learned how to control the PC with the installed MetaTrader 4 Client Terminal via PDA.

mechanism: Compute classic/Woodie/Camarilla/DeMark pivots from prior period H,L,C (and O variants); for FX, redefine the period via GMT-aligned session/day using DailyPivot_Shift so server-time candlestick boundaries do not distort High/Low/Close of the analytical day; snap computed R/S to nearest historical chart levels.
data_needed: Prior-session High, Low, Close (Open optional); GMT vs terminal-time offset; H1 bars for reconstructing the shifted day.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPUSD pivot sensitivity table; EURJPY intraday S/R narrative; session/day period; H1 for GMT correction; weekends skipped on Mondays.
why_new_for_mis: Makes session pivots a reproducible overnight reference sensor under multi-session FX clocks rather than broker-server midnight artifacts.
quote: To exclude the situation when the internal terminal time influences calculations, it is necessary to use one-hour candlesticks corrected for the difference between the terminal time and GMT.

mechanism: MetaQuotes survey on mobile terminal satisfaction and feature wishes—product research, not sensing.
quote: the functionalities and features that are currently incorporated in the mobile terminals offered by MetaQuotes Software Corp. are fully satisfying the needs of 92% of its users.

mechanism: EA reports each open/close via DLL into shared memory: Action, PriceOpen/Close, Slippage, TimeForOpen/Close, Requotes (retry count). Monitor aggregates mean slippage, requote rates, and execution duration across brokers/symbols to rank venues for a given EA.
data_needed: Per-trade intended vs fill price, timestamps at send and fill, requote/retry counts, broker id (AccountServer), symbol digits.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Multi-broker MT4 terminals; demo EA on any symbol with bar-direction entries and TimeInMarket exits; live multi-terminal comparison.
why_new_for_mis: Treats broker microstructure (slippage, requotes, latency) as measurable liquidity/execution quality sensors, not only as static broker choice.
quote: Analyzing the statistic (number of requotes, time of a trade execution, slippage) and viewing all trades we can conclude, with what brokerage company it is better to work.

mechanism: Derives that doubling-to-double-capital martingale yields P(win)=1/2 same as betting all capital; demo EA with random direction and equal SL/TP—MM math, not market sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex EA with fixed 0.1 lot start, random long/short, equal SL/TP distance.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: martingale probability critique only.
quote: using the Martingale does not provide any advantages; we could as well bet all our capital Q and the winning probability would be the same (1/2).

mechanism: Do not feed raw quotes Ct to nets (strong lag-1 correlation C(t+1)≈C(t)); use delta(C) or log(C(t)/C(t+1)) for more statistically independent, inflation-stationary inputs so training uses longer history with stable scale.
data_needed: Close (or mid) series transformed to increments or log-ratios; train/test split.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EUR exported from MT4 archive; daily closes arranged as 4 prior → next close; euro.zip sample.
why_new_for_mis: Codifies a preprocessing sensor layer (returns/log-ratios) that MIS neural/sequence models should use instead of raw price levels.
quote: as entries and exits one should not use the values of quotes Ct. What is really significant is the quotes' changes.

mechanism: Fixed lag windows miss far extrema that still matter to traders, while widening windows blows up net dimension; wavelet decomposition keeps information equivalent to lag immersion but compresses the past with selective accuracy—farther history kept as coarser form of the curve.
data_needed: Price series wavelet coefficients with multi-scale compression of distant history.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Financial time series / FX forecasting context; long histories where inflation and far extrema matter.
why_new_for_mis: Offers MIS a multi-scale sequence encoding that expands effective lookback without proportional input dimension growth.
quote: A quite promising tool here can be a wavelet decomposition. In terms of informativity it is equal to the lag immersion, but easier accepts such data compression, which describes the past with the selective accuracy.

mechanism: Matlab ANFIS: 4 lagged closes as inputs, each with 3 triangular membership functions, linear output MFs; hybrid (or backprop) training on ~60 in-sample days then test on next 9 days—multilayer hybrid neuro-fuzzy net forecasting absolute next close (author notes experts prefer not using raw quotes).
data_needed: MT4-exported OHLC CSV→Excel lag table (4 prior closes → next close); train vs out-of-sample split; ANFIS FIS structure.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EUR daily closes from MetaTrader quotes archive; 60 train / 9 test days; OOS RMSE ~32 points.
why_new_for_mis: Concrete neuro-fuzzy sequence sensor for short-horizon price forecast, integrable to MT via DLL—baseline neural sensing path for MIS.
quote: The result of our work is the multilayer hybrid neural network that can forecast absolute price values for the near future.

mechanism: For each closed trade record MAE (max adverse excursion) and MFE (max favorable excursion) in points or money; scatter vs final return and fit Correlation(Profits,MAE)/Correlation(Profits,MFE) to detect sit-out-of-losses vs premature TP behavior—path-quality sensing during trade life, not just final P&L.
data_needed: Per-trade high-water adverse and favorable floating P&L (or price excursion) from open to close; final return.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Automated Trading Championship 2006 accounts (e.g. RobinHood MAE −$120 to −$2500); multi-pair money terms if mixed symbols.
why_new_for_mis: Adds intra-trade adverse/favorable excursion distributions as sensors of path risk and profit-capture quality beyond closed-trade stats.
quote: MFE shows the maximal price movement in a favorable direction. Respectively, MAE shows the maximal price movement in an adverse direction.

mechanism: Z=(N*(R-0.5)-P)/sqrt(P*(P-N)/(N-1)) with P=2*W*L on the +/- trade-outcome sequence; |Z| large vs normal implies dependence—negative Z → runs of wins/losses (positive dependence), positive Z → alternation (negative dependence)—usable to gate size or skip trades.
data_needed: Ordered sequence of profitable vs losing closed trades; counts N, W, L, and run count R.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Championship 2006 accounts (e.g. Rich Z=-3.85 from clustered same-direction MACD entries); any trade log.
why_new_for_mis: Sequence sensor on trade-outcome dependence, complementary to market-price neural/regime sensors.
quote: Z-score of a trading sequence may inform us about possible dependence between consecutive trades.

mechanism: EA places up/down arrows each new bar; user deletes one within time_limit; scores Open→Close direction forecasts to a CSV—human intuition trainer, not an automated market sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Any Symbol()/Period(); author mentions M5 streaks of 5–10 correct.
why_new_for_mis: Full read: training game for discretionary direction calls, no MIS sensing algorithm.
quote: If we use betting in the form of a game on small timeframes, we can develop our "market intuition".
